title: Why Do Onions Make You Cry?
summary: Chopping an onion sets off a tiny chemical chain reaction that ends with a gas your eyes hate. Here is how it works, and why the tears are a defence.

beats.text: You slice an onion and your eyes start streaming. Is it the juice, a gas, or heat?

visual.text: Why do onions make you cry?

beats.text: Inside an onion, two chemicals sit in separate pockets. A knife breaks the walls between them.
Once they mix, a quick reaction starts. What reaches your eyes?
beats.reveal: A gas! It floats up from the board and stings your eyes.

beats.text: Your eyes sting, so they flood with tears to wash it away. Crying is a cleaning job.
Fewer tears? Chill the onion first. The cold slows the reaction down.
Bonus fact: the gas is the onion's defence. Nothing wants to bite something that stings.

visual.text: The onion's gas is a natural defence against animals that might eat it.
